Hi Elena — thanks and great questions. I’ve started populating the questionnaire focusing on technical controls and data flows; high-level answers below and I’ll attach a completed copy shortly: 

- Controller/Processor: We confirm Redwood acts as a processor for the inference requests and does not make independent decisions about the purposes of processing customer data.
- SCC Module: Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor) from the 2021 SCCs aligns with our standard DPA. We are prepared to adopt that module; if you need C2C mapping we can discuss legal implications.
- Subprocessors: We use a limited set of subprocessors (compute and logging providers). Redwood provides a public subprocessors list and gives 30 days’ notice for material changes; emergency changes come with prompt notification and justification.
- Retention: Default logs for debugging are retained 30 days by default; customers can request shorter retention windows. We retain model cache slices only for request-scoped inference and do not store persistent copies of customer prompts beyond configured retention.
- Deletion: We support per-customer data deletion requests and will provide API endpoints for formal deletions; we’ll document the SLA in the DPA.

Action items from us:
- Complete questionnaire (attached) — target Wed 2026-03-04 EOD.
- Coordinate with Laura on DPA language for SCC insertion.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood DPA v1 (draft) + recommended SCC module mapping

Elena — attaching our DPA draft for your legal team’s review (Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf). Key highlights and recommendations below: 

- SCC insertion: We recommend using the 2021 Standard Contractual Clauses Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor). We included the full SCC text as an annex and a redline placeholder where your counsel can toggle alternative modules if needed.
- Data categories: The DPA defines data categories as: contact data, support case content (may include limited PII), and metadata (timestamps, case IDs).
- Subprocessors & notice: Section 4.2 provides our subprocessors list and commits to 30 days’ notice. Emergency subprocessors are covered under Section 4.3 with expedited notification.
- Retention & deletion: Section 5 sets a default 30-day debug log retention, with contractual options down to 7 days for enterprise customers. Deletion requests are scannable via API and entitle you to confirmation within 10 business days.
- Audit rights: We offer SOC 2 report sharing under NDA and have an operational audit window; full on-site audits can be negotiated for enterprise plans.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Finovexa legal to review DPA and confirm SCC Module 2 is acceptable.
2) Finovexa to confirm whether you need reduced retention or any additional controls.
3) Return of the populated questionnaire by EOD Wed 2026-03-04 so we can finalize the DPA for signature.

I’ve attached an SCC_Comparison_Matrix.xlsx that maps the choices and impacts. Happy to hop on a short call if the legal teams prefer to walk through live.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
